SCOPE, and why these exact ticks: the tick list is not a guess or a window. Each entry is a PAIR START (head-1) whose divergence DEMONSTRABLY VANISHES when this site's damage is emulated (MGC_BUILD_DAT_DAMAGE, dig D14's instrument): measured 58 devs -> 33 with the substitution, and these are exactly the 28 heads present in the un-emulated run and absent from the emulated one. ALL FOUR of mc1l6's heads are this one wound, read by TWO different readers: the (10,42) castle PAINTER sub_285C0 raises 5 cells the port does not (heads t=11781 at site (12,24) and t=28754 at site (3,227)), and the castle-DEMOLISH walker sub_28FE0 razes those same 5 cells, whose per-cell wall arm draws the LCG -- so retail's collapse spends MORE draws and every downstream per-cell depth in the 35x35 rect shifts by a small signed amount (heads t=22561 and t=27826, 435 and 420 height cells apart in a single tick). Entities standing on the drifted ground then read the wrong z, which is why all four heads are `z` across UNRELATED classes -- (9,1) slot 529, (5,15) slots 250/320/478, (10,0) slot 164. THE PROOFS. (1) THE PORT IS BYTE-FAITHFUL: the goal decode was disassembled out of the shipped CARPET.EXE (sub_285C0 = file 0x40DB8; classify `cmp cl,0xf` at 0x288BD, the <0xF arm at 0x288C2, the >=0xF arm at 0x288E7 -- `cl % 16`, `(lo-1) << 2`, `+ target(z>>5)`, `- height`), and it matches the port's `fill_castle_goal_row` exactly; the inner-row rect geometry differs from the port's ONLY in the +4/+5 axis transposition, which is VACUOUS here because every castle course (build_tab rows 1..8) is SQUARE. (2) THE ASSET IS NOT REACHABLE: goal = target+56 requires a cell byte with low nibble 15, and build rows 1..5 of the shipped BUILD0-0.DAT contain ZERO such bytes anywhere -- yet retail applied exactly target+56 at three cells, in three separate builds, at two sites. (3) IT IS ROW 5 AND ONLY ROW 5: the take's five level-1..4 castle builds (t=2291/2386/2522/2580/2700/2774/.../11651) are BIT-EXACT on the height plane, and the collapse walker's draw count -- graded against RETAIL'S OWN LCG via pool slot 0's `+4` (MGC_COLLAPSE_PROBE) -- is EXACT for rows 4/3/2/1 (99/317/100/26) and SHORT for row 5 twice (port 895 v retail 899 at t=22560; port 864 v retail 869 at t=27814). Those are the '2 draw-count mismatches' the companion rule already cites as its clinching site-selectivity argument. (4) THE FIVE-BYTE SUBSTITUTION CLOSES THE TAKE: with MGC_BUILD_DAT_DAMAGE="12,24:2736=5B,2737=5F,2738=5F,2739=5F,2750=54" mc1l6 goes 5 segments / 4 excess resets / segmented horizon 11,780 -> 2 segments / 1 excess reset / horizon 28,753, BOTH collapse draw counts land on retail's exact 899 and 869, and cells (13,17)/(14,17)/(15,17)/(16,17) become bit-exact on height AND type AND angle; pointing the SAME five bytes at the other site ("3,227:...2750=57") closes head t=28754 instead. ⭐⭐⭐ FACTS ABOUT THE CLASS FROM THIS TAKE. ⚠ CORRECTED BY THE MAIN SESSION 2026-09-09: the dig originally claimed the damaged VALUE CHANGES MID-RUN; re-measurement REFUTES that. The damage is PER-INSTANCE and CONSTANT IN TIME -- each castle stamp carries its own damaged image. Measured: the site-(12,24) fit closes EXACTLY heads 11781+22561+27826, and the site-(3,227) fit closes EXACTLY head 28754; the two are DISJOINT AND COMPLEMENTARY and together account for all four. What made it look time-varying is that MGC_BUILD_DAT_DAMAGE is SITE-SCOPED (one site per run), so no single invocation can close the take. The fit is also UNIQUE, not a best fit: a 16-value sweep of byte 2750 at site (12,24) yields horizon 28,753 for 0x54 and 11,797 for every other value. This makes the class PER-INSTANCE SELECTIVE, which is stronger evidence for data damage over a code defect than round 121's per-process argument. (a) THE 'AFTER EACH RELOAD' CAUSE IS REFUTED AGAIN: mc1l6 has ZERO respawns and ZERO restarts (replay reports `0 respawn(s), 0 suicide(s)`), so this damage was acquired in ordinary play -- round 121 called round 118's reload cause doubtful; this is an independent witness on a different level and a different build row. A static asset difference cannot do that; only live memory can. SCOPE: the four ticks are PAIR STARTS (head-1) of the four measured heads and nothing else; the reconstructed byte VALUES are a best fit, not unique, exactly as in the companion rule. ⚠ The height plane is an UNGRADED lane, so the residual terrain drift this rule does not excuse is invisible to both graded channels -- see the W6 unit test `engine::features::tests::the_level5_castle_course_paints_only_the_shipped_bytes`.
